releases.title: What you type stays put

highlights.title: No more vanishing text
highlights.text: With the phone line on, what you typed in any field was wiped every 20 seconds. It now stays.

highlights.title: Quiet checks stay quiet
highlights.text: The phone line and the planning diary are still checked in the background, but the screen only changes when something new arrives.

highlights.title: Your place kept
highlights.text: When a new call does arrive, the screen updates around you: your text, the field you're in and the cursor stay where they were.

changes: The background phone-line check saves and redraws only when a call arrives or the line's status changes; its spinner shows only for Check line
The planning diary refresh redraws only when the diary is different
Every redraw keeps the fields you've edited, the focus and the cursor; a field is let go once its value is saved, and a form opened afresh starts empty
Tests: 20-background-typing, which fails on 1.8.0 (26 of 26 with the testkit)
fixes: With the phone line set up, text typed in any field was reset every 20 seconds

releases.title: Register someone without a call

highlights.title: Register at the desk
highlights.text: Someone at the desk, or a call you took yourself: add them with their details and what they need, in one step.

highlights.title: Straight to booking
highlights.text: The request waits in To book marked Front desk and opens into the booking box with a time already suggested.

highlights.title: A new request any time
highlights.text: New request on a client's page books them again without asking their details.

changes: Register someone (front desk) and Add (Patients): name, phone, age where the business asks, a note, and an optional request to book: what they need, service (or let Frontly suggest), urgency 1–5, best time
New request on a client's page, for someone already on record
A front-desk request gets a note like a call's (triage, service and person), is marked ✎ Front desk on cards and in the case, and has no call to read
Editing and registering share the same checks: a name, a phone number of 6 digits or more that no other record has, an age from 0 to 120
Tests: 19-register (25 of 25 with the testkit)

releases.title: Import clients and staff

highlights.title: Bring your lists in
highlights.text: Settings › Data › Import: a CSV file or rows copied from a spreadsheet, for clients or staff, with columns in English or Lithuanian.

highlights.title: A preview first
highlights.text: See who's new, who's already here and which rows are skipped and why. Nothing is saved until you tap Import.

highlights.title: Patients from ClinicCards
highlights.text: With ClinicCards set up, its window imports your patients too, linked to their ClinicCards records.

changes: Import window: Choose a file… or paste; comma, semicolon or tab; quoted text; headers like name, first/last name, phone, age, birth date, notes, role, services, days, hours, or vardas, pavardė, telefonas, gimimo data, pastabos, pareigos, paslaugos
Clients are matched by phone number, staff by name ("Dr." or not); records already here are kept as they are and get a missing age or the engine's id
Staff rows: services matched to yours, days such as Mon-Fri, Mon;Wed;Fri or Pr-Pn, hours such as 8-16; an unknown service is pointed out
Planning engines may offer clients() for Import patients; ClinicCards reads its patients page by page
Import from Settings › Data, from the empty client list, and from the ClinicCards window
Tests: 18-import (24 of 24 with the testkit)

releases.title: Book into ClinicCards

highlights.title: Planning engines
highlights.text: Settings › Planning: book in Frontly's own diary, or straight into ClinicCards. More planning services can plug in the same way.

highlights.title: A window for each
highlights.text: ClinicCards has its own settings: the API key, a connection test, the cabinet, the note, and which ClinicCards person each of your staff is.

highlights.title: Real free times
highlights.text: With ClinicCards in use, the times come from its shifts minus its visits, and a booking is checked and made there first.

changes: A pluggable planning-engine layer: each engine is one entry with its settings fields, its secret, what it can't do, and test, staff, diary and book calls (docs/INTEGRATIONS.md)
ClinicCards: Token-header API; staff, cabinets, booking step, shifts, visits and blocked time read; patient found by full-digit number or created; a BOOKING visit made; the time re-checked live first
Each engine's own settings window: API key in the Keychain, Test, its options, staff links, Import (links by name, "Dr." or not), Use; can't be used before a test
Booking box and calendar use the engine's diary; a person not linked says so; the engine's errors are shown and nothing is kept
Cancelling or moving a visit booked in ClinicCards reminds you to do it there too (its API has no call for it)
Tests: 17-cliniccards with the API faked as the 4WP Booking connector uses it (23 of 23 with the testkit)

releases.title: Edit a client's details

highlights.title: Edit details
highlights.text: Fix a name, a phone number or an age on the client's page. The new name shows everywhere and reaches the phone line at once.

highlights.title: One number, one client
highlights.text: Reva recognises callers by their number, so Frontly won't let two records share one, and says who already has it.

highlights.title: Remove a record
highlights.text: Take a record away when it's not needed; Frontly won't while a booking is ahead, and the calls stay.

changes: A client's page: Edit details (name, phone, age where the business asks for it), Save, Cancel, Remove; mistakes are explained and what was typed stays
The record's name is the name shown on cards and the case, ahead of the name said on a call
The phone bridge gets the patient list again after an edit or a removal
Tests: 16-edit-client (22 of 22 with the testkit)
fixes: A misspelt name from a call could only be fixed by a new call

releases.title: A new logo for any front desk

highlights.title: A request that becomes a booking
highlights.text: The new logo is a speech bubble shaped like a calendar page, with a teal check for booked and a pink dot for a new call.

highlights.title: For any business
highlights.text: No tooth any more: the logo fits a clinic, a car service or any office.

highlights.title: Everywhere at once
highlights.text: The app header, the launch animation, the widget and the app icon all show it.

changes: New logo: frame (two sound marks), drawing (a speech bubble with calendar rings and a header line), pop (a pink new-call dot), sweep (a teal check); the launch animation draws it in the same four steps
docs/logo.svg and the 1024 px app icon redrawn; the widget fetches the new icon with this version
README: banner (with a voice waveform instead of a heartbeat line), header text, every screenshot and the GIF wall redone

releases.title: Any kind of office

highlights.title: Pick your kind of business
highlights.text: Settings › Business: a dental clinic, a car service, or any office. Each brings its own words, services and the questions Reva asks.

highlights.title: Your own words
highlights.text: Call your staff mechanics, consultants or anything else, your callers customers or clients, and add the services you offer.

highlights.title: The dental demo, as it was
highlights.text: The dental clinic keeps its questions, its safety rule and Reva's phone instructions word for word, so the phone line needs no changes.

changes: Templates: Dental clinic (unchanged), Car service (the problem, the car, whether it can be driven; smoke, fuel or brake safety), Office or other service (reason, urgency, best time)

Each template: the words for staff, callers, bookings and the place; its services and how calls are routed to them; the script's questions in English and Lithuanian; the AI's wording; the AI voice's style
Settings › Business: kind of business, your own words (one and many), services to add and remove, Reset; staff are moved to services that exist when the template changes
Every screen, the case, the calendar, the tabs and the settings use the business's words; the call details show only what the business asks
Reva's phone instructions follow the template with the same bridge variables; the surgery gap shows only for a dental clinic; a setting for where the business is
Tests: 15-business-templates (21 of 21 with the testkit), including a word-for-word check of the dental instructions; node bridge/test.mjs 14 checks

releases.title: A tidier front desk bar

highlights.title: Real buttons
highlights.text: Check line is now a proper button with a phone icon, and shows a spinner while it checks.

highlights.title: Who's signed in
highlights.text: The receptionist shows with their initials and today's bookings, on one line that never wraps.

highlights.title: Sign out
highlights.text: A round button at the end of the bar, out of the way of Check line.

changes: Front desk bar: the receptionist with initials and "Booked today", a Check line pill (phone icon, spinner while checking), a round Sign out button; nothing wraps onto two lines
Tests: 10-phone-line checks the bar's buttons (20 of 20 with the testkit)
fixes: Check line and Sign out were plain links that broke onto two lines

releases.title: Your clinic, your dentists

highlights.title: Add your dentists
highlights.text: Settings › Dentists: add each dentist with their role, what they do, their days and hours. Bookings, suggestions and the calendar use them.

highlights.title: No made-up data
highlights.text: No invented patients fill the diary any more, and the demo patients are gone: the calendar and the front desk show only your calls and bookings.

highlights.title: Better calendar buttons
highlights.text: Round buttons with clear arrows step through days, weeks and months, and Back to today brings you home.

changes: Settings › Dentists: add, edit and remove; a dentist with visits booked can't be removed, one with only past visits is hidden so the history still names them
An install that already booked with the five sample dentists keeps them, now editable; a new install starts with none and points to Settings › Dentists
The made-up patients that filled the diary are gone, and so is Settings › Booking › Demo: slots already taken; the calendar counts only bookings
The three demo patients and their call are removed once; real phone calls stay, and a demo record a real call was filed under keeps that call and its booking
Settings › Demo › Start the demo again becomes Settings › Data › Remove all calls and patients
Trends say so when there is nothing to show yet
Tests: 13-dentists, 14-no-demo-data (20 of 20 with the testkit); node bridge/test.mjs 14 checks
fixes: The calendar's arrow buttons were small and their arrows sat off-centre

releases.title: Smarter booking, and the clinic at a glance

highlights.title: Calendar
highlights.text: A new tab shows how full the clinic is: each dentist's day, the week and the month as percent taken, and trends with the busiest days and dentists.

highlights.title: A time that fits
highlights.text: Each call opens with a suggested time already selected: the right dentist, what the caller asked for ("after 3 pm", "Friday"), sooner when it's urgent. The AI weighs in when there's judgement to make.

highlights.title: Visits that make sense
highlights.text: A patient's visits never overlap and are kept apart, two surgeries leave time to heal, and a change of booking moves the visit instead of adding a second one.

changes: Front desk: a patient with several calls in a list gets one stacked card with all of them and their booked visits
Booking rules (Settings › Booking): days between a patient's visits (1) and between two surgeries (14); times that break them are struck through, with the reason
Suggested time from the caller's preference (hours, weekdays, tomorrow, next week), the note's dentist and the urgency; preselected
AI plan: picks from the allowed free times, explains why, warns, and offers alternatives; asked automatically for other visits, surgery or a change
A change of booking: Visit to move, then Move to …; the old visit is marked moved and its call shows where it went
Calendar tab: Day (each dentist's times), Week (heat grid), Month, Trends (weekly occupancy, busiest weekdays, dentists for the next two weeks, calls per day, four figures and three observations)
The made-up diary is busier on Mondays and mid-mornings and fills up nearer the day, so the calendar looks like a clinic's
Tests: 12-booking-rules (18 of 18 with the testkit); node bridge/test.mjs 14 checks
fixes: A change of booking was booked as a second visit next to the first
A preferred time on a card was cut off in the middle of a number

releases.title: Returning callers, handled

highlights.title: "When is my visit?"
highlights.text: Reva knows each patient's booked visits and answers when, what time and with which dentist, without adding anything to the front desk's list.

highlights.title: Only real booking work waits
highlights.text: Questions go to Other, filed under the patient. A patient who calls again about a request that's waiting is added to it ("Called 2×") instead of queueing twice.

highlights.title: Messages for the patient
highlights.text: Write a message on the patient's page; Reva passes it on at their next call and Frontly marks it as passed on.

changes: Each phone call has a purpose: new visit, question about a booked visit, change to a booked visit, or other; from the agent's new intent field, Frontly's AI note, or the call itself
Front desk: Closed becomes Other (closed calls and calls that needed no booking); cards show the purpose and how many times someone called; a filed call can be moved to To book
Patient page: a message for the patient, its history once passed on, and each call's purpose
The patient brief for the bridge adds booked visits, a waiting request and the message; Reva's instructions (Settings › Phone line › Copy) use them
bridge: new variables patient_appointments, patient_waiting, patient_message, patient_message_id; reads the intent and message_passed fields
Tests: 11-returning-caller (17 of 17 with the testkit); node bridge/test.mjs 14 checks
fixes: Short labels on the front-desk cards broke onto two lines; they now stay whole and move to the next row, and only long warnings wrap
A patient who phoned twice about the same thing showed up twice in To book

releases.title: The caller's language from the first word

highlights.title: Language by phone number
highlights.text: A +370 number hears Reva in Lithuanian, a +371 number in Latvian and any other country in English, from her very first word.

highlights.title: Greetings in three languages
highlights.text: Reva's opening, including "Ar tai Jonas?" for a known patient, now comes in Lithuanian, Latvian or English.

highlights.title: Updated instructions
highlights.text: Copy Reva's instructions again from Settings › Phone line: they now start in the caller's language and switch if the caller answers in another.

changes: bridge: the call-start answer picks the language from the caller's country code, then the number dialled, then LANGUAGE; it sends the agent-language override and a {{call_language}} variable
bridge: a Latvian opening line; Twilio's stand-in numbers for hidden callers are recognised; LANGUAGE_OVERRIDE=off for agents with the override switched off
Reva's instructions (Settings › Phone line › Copy) use {{call_language}} instead of a fixed Lithuanian-or-English rule
Tests: 16 of 16 with the testkit; node bridge/test.mjs 14 checks (Latvian, foreign and hidden callers, the override switch)
fixes: Calls always started in the agent's default language, whatever number called

releases.title: Notes that fit the screen

highlights.title: Long warnings wrap
highlights.text: A long warning or label in a call note now wraps onto the next line inside the card instead of running off the screen.

highlights.title: No sideways scrolling
highlights.text: The case sheet and the app's pages stay exactly the width of the screen, so nothing can be dragged sideways by accident.

highlights.title: Ready for real calls
highlights.text: Notes written from real phone calls, which tend to carry longer warnings, now read cleanly at the front desk.

changes: Pills (urgency, priority, specialty, warnings) may wrap within the card's width; warnings keep the ⚠ at the top of a wrapped line
The page, its sheets and the note box no longer allow horizontal scrolling; very long words break inside the box
Tests: 10-phone-line checks the wrapping and no-sideways-scroll rules (16 of 16 with the testkit); node bridge/test.mjs still 11 checks
fixes: A long AI warning in a call note ran past the right edge and let the case sheet scroll sideways

releases.title: A real phone number for Reva

highlights.title: Call Reva for real
highlights.text: Connect a Twilio number answered by an ElevenLabs agent: Reva picks up real calls, and the Call tab dials the number for you.

highlights.title: Real calls at the front desk
highlights.text: Calls the line took arrive by themselves, marked 📞, filed under the caller's record with the transcript, the details and a note, ready to book.

highlights.title: She knows who's calling
highlights.text: A known number gets a greeting by name and Reva knows the last visit, because Frontly shares a short patient list with your bridge.

changes: Settings › Phone line: the bridge address, its token (settings blueprint secrets: Keychain, native prompt, Make one), status, Check now, and Reva's instructions for ElevenLabs to copy

Frontly checks the bridge 1.5 s after opening and every 20 s while open; new calls are imported once, matched to patients by number, and get Frontly's AI note when a key is set, otherwise ElevenLabs' summary
bridge/: a Cloudflare Worker (call-start lookup for ElevenLabs, HMAC-verified post-call webhook, calls for Frontly, the patient brief) with its own tests and a step-by-step setup guide
The scripted Lithuanian greeting for a known patient is now "Ar tai …?", which works with any name
Tests: 10-phone-line (16 of 16 with the testkit), node bridge/test.mjs (11 checks)
fixes: The Lithuanian greeting put a name in the wrong case ("Ar kalbu su Jonas?")

releases.title: Patients, organised

highlights.title: Grouped by what needs doing
highlights.text: Patients sort into To book, Visit booked, New and everyone else, or by last contact or name.

highlights.title: Filters and search
highlights.text: Show only callers to book, booked visits or new patients, with a count on each, and search by name or number.

highlights.title: More on every card
highlights.text: The next visit with its dentist or the open call with its urgency, plus visits, calls, notes, mood, and a warning when two records share a number.

changes: The Patients tab is rebuilt: grouping (remembered as settings.patGroup), filters with counts, full-width cards with status rings
Tests: 09-patients-list: 15 of 15
fixes: Patient rows shrank to their text and sat centred at different widths

releases.title: Lithuanian calls, hands free

highlights.title: Lithuanian works
highlights.text: iPhone dictation has no Lithuanian, so Reva now hears you through OpenAI transcription, or asks you to type when there's no OpenAI key.

highlights.title: Just stop talking
highlights.text: With OpenAI transcription, Reva stops listening on her own when you pause and sends your answer. No tap needed.

highlights.title: Easier to read
highlights.text: The receptionist's name under the clinic on the call screen is readable in every colour scheme.

changes: When iPhone dictation says a language isn't supported, Frontly remembers it (settings.noDictation) and uses OpenAI transcription for that language, or the keyboard without an OpenAI key; Settings › Calls and the Call tab say so
OpenAI transcription ends each answer by itself after a pause (Settings › Calls › Stop listening after a pause of, 1.2 s), after 10 s of silence, or after 45 s
Tests: 07-no-dictation and 08-transcribe-hands-free (a fake microphone) join the testkit run: 14 of 14
fixes: A Lithuanian call showed iOS's raw "Dictation is not supported for the locale lt-LT" and stopped listening
An answer transcribed by OpenAI was dropped instead of reaching Reva
The line under the clinic's name on the call screen was nearly invisible

releases.title: Meet Reva, the virtual receptionist

highlights.title: Call the clinic
highlights.text: Ring a demo dental clinic from your iPhone. Reva answers, asks what's wrong, how much it hurts and when you can come, and you answer by voice or by typing.

highlights.title: A note ready to book
highlights.text: Every call ends with a note for the front desk: urgency, red flags, the right dentist and, with AI, how the caller sounded.

highlights.title: Be the receptionist
highlights.text: Sign in to the front desk, work the queue most urgent first, and book each caller into a free slot with the right dentist.

changes: First release: the Call tab (known patients recognised by phone number, new callers get a record), the live call screen with Reva's notes filling in, the Front desk queue and booking, and Patients
Reva follows a script in English or Lithuanian without AI; with a Claude or OpenAI key she holds a real conversation, reads the caller's mood and writes the note
With an OpenAI key Reva can speak with an AI voice and callers can be transcribed by OpenAI; otherwise an iPhone voice and iPhone dictation

Blueprints: Stability patterns 1.0.2, In-app updates 1.1.1, Settings 2.0.1, AI configuration 1.0.2, Launch screen 1.0.2, Widgets 1.1.1, AI invitation 1.2.2, Sound in silent mode 1.0.2; recipes: safe start-up 1.1.0, portable bridge 1.0.0, testing 1.2.2
